object: Whether EvoDRC connectivity/admissibility gate status identifies positive local DRC utility for records persisted into skill-evolution history.
structural_findings: EvoDRC copies one repair record into every touched-layer history, so the simpler explanation 'credit is written only to the wrong target layer' is ruled out.
For unit_gate records, connectivity/admissibility can be accepted while local DRC utility is absent from the persisted record; the record instead carries shared block-level start/end outcome context.
The same history.jsonl records are fed to later skill generation/judging as measured evidence.
Therefore gated_in is a feasibility/admissibility predicate, not an identified positive-utility label.

first_party_witnesses.interpretation: The record survives into persistent skill material, but released skill text can use such evidence both as caution and as an operational example; the audit therefore does not claim blind promotion of every locally harmful record.

safe_conclusion: The released EvoDRC substrate directly demonstrates that connectivity/admissibility and local causal/utility polarity are different labels. This is evidence for a credit-semantics mismatch, not evidence that the mismatch is novel or that it dominates EvoDRC's final performance.
not_claimed: EvoDRC skill evolution is harmful overall
locally harmful trials are always promoted as successful skill rules
the observed credit ambiguity is a new causal primitive
